answers_by_date.answer: Convictions do not affect citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: In force: Ley 346 as restored by Ley 23.059 (1984), and Decreto 3213/84. Neither has a ground for loss of acquired citizenship because of a conviction. Art. 8 Ley 346 only suspends political rights for those under sentence of 'pena infamante o de muerte'. Art. 16 Decreto 3213/84 says this suspension 'no priva de los derechos ni exime de las obligaciones inherentes a la nacionalidad argentina, sea ésta nativa o adquirida'. Annulment is limited to fraud (arts. 10, 15, 18). The loss grounds of Ley de facto 21.795 had been repealed, and the losses under it voided, by Ley 23.059 in 1984. I found no documented case of a naturalised person losing citizenship for a conviction. Practice evidence for this period is thin.

answers_by_date.answer: Convictions do not affect citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: Same texts as in 2000. Decreto 1601/2004 (B.O. 19/11/2004) replaced only art. 2 of Decreto 3213/84 (the option procedure for children of native Argentines) and did not touch arts. 15, 16 or 18. Ley 25.871 (in force from January 2004) governs foreigners, not citizens. I found no practice evidence of conviction-based loss.

answers_by_date.answer: Convictions do not affect citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: No change to Ley 346 arts. 8 and 9 or to Decreto 3213/84 arts. 15, 16 and 18. Decreto 616/2010 (May 2010) regulates migration, not citizenship. I found no documented loss for a conviction.

answers_by_date.answer: Convictions do not affect citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 26.774 (B.O. 02/11/2012) amended only art. 7 Ley 346 (voting age 16). DNU 70/2017 later amended only art. 2 inc. 1 (acquisition), not loss. The regime stayed fraud-only through 1 January 2020. I found no practice evidence of conviction-based loss.

answers.notes: The protection rests on statutory silence plus Decreto 3213/84 art. 16, which separates the art. 8 suspension of political rights from nationality. Only fraud can annul a naturalisation (outside this indicator). The 'Effectively Always' rating is inferred from the absence of any documented loss, not from affirmative practice reports.

answers_by_date.basis: In force: Constitution art. 20 ('Obtienen nacionalización residiendo dos años continuos en la Nación') and Ley 346 art. 2 inc. 1 in its 1869 text ('Los estranjeros mayores de 18 años, que residiesen en la República dos años continuos y manifestasen ante los jueces federales de sección su voluntad de serlo'), restored by Ley 23.059. Decreto 3213/84 art. 3 sets the same conditions and the bars (no honest means of support, pending prosecution, a doloso conviction over 3 years). Naturalisation was handled by federal courts. I found no practice evidence for 2000. The rating carries the starting level forward; confidence is low.

Same texts. Ley 25.871 replaced Ley 22.439 in January 2004 but does not regulate naturalisation. Courts were split on whether the two years had to be lawful residence; this mainly affects irregular migrants, not regular economic migrants. I found no specific practice data for 2005.

Same texts. On 23 June 2009 the CSJN ('Ni, I-Hsing', Fallos 332:1466) held that the art. 20 / Ley 346 residence requirement does not require lawful migration status. It reversed a Córdoba chamber that had denied citizenship. I know this ruling only from secondary sources and treat it as practice evidence: courts mostly grant naturalisation, and the CSJN corrects restrictive lower-court readings.

Ley 346 art. 2 inc. 1 was still in its 1869 text; DNU 70/2017 changed it only from 31 January 2017. Before 1 January 2020 that change narrowed the route to residence 'como residentes permanentes o temporarios' under migration law, which economic migrants with residence permits satisfy. Practice up to 2020: lower courts sometimes added unwritten requirements. In Liu Cairong the La Plata chamber required Spanish; the CSJN reversed on 11 February 2020.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

answers.starting_answer_concern: The answer holds. However, on 1 January 2020 art. 2 inc. 1 Ley 346 was in its DNU 70/2017 form, requiring permanent or temporary residence, not the plain constitutional formula the MRD quotes. The pathway still existed for regular economic migrants.

The answer is 'Yes' at every date. Rulings are used as practice evidence because I did not read them in full. The 2025 investment route and the move to DNM processing are outside the period.

answers_by_date.basis: Refugees had no specific naturalisation route. They used the general route of Constitution art. 20, Ley 346 art. 2 inc. 1 (two years' residence of any kind, 1869 text) and Decreto 3213/84 art. 3. Refugee status was then governed by CEPARE decrees, which I did not read. I found no practice evidence on refugee naturalisation around 2000; confidence is low.
Same general route. Ley 26.165 had not yet been enacted (B.O. 01/12/2006). I found no practice evidence for refugees or asylum seekers in this period.

Ley 26.165 (2006) incorporates the 1951 Convention (art. 1) but has no naturalisation provision. The general Ley 346 route applied, and the 2009 CSJN Ni I-Hsing ruling held that lawful status was not required. I found no refugee-specific practice evidence.

Unchanged until DNU 70/2017 (31 January 2017) required permanent or temporary residence. Recognised refugees with residence permits still qualify; asylum seekers holding only a 'residencia precaria' could not count that time. A later case (Ndiaye, La Plata 2023) shows a lower court refusing an asylum seeker whose application began in December 2018. That is thin evidence and about asylum seekers only.

answers.notes: There is no humanitarian-specific naturalisation clause in Argentine law between 2000 and 2020; the pathway is the general one. Art. 34 of the 1951 Convention (facilitate naturalisation) applies through Ley 26.165 art. 1 from 2006; it is not a separate statutory route. answers_by_date.basis: In force: Constitution art. 20 and Ley 346 art. 2 inc. 1 (two years). Ley 346 art. 2 inc. 2 point 7 gives a route 'cualquiera que sea el tiempo de su residencia' to a man married to an Argentine woman ('Haberse casado con mujer argentina'). Decreto 3213/84 art. 3 reformulates this gender-neutrally: 'f) tener cónyuge o hijo argentino nativo'. I found no practice evidence for 2000.

The practice evidence is general (lower-court extra requirements later corrected by the CSJN), not family-specific.

answers.sourcing_note: The 1869 text of art. 2 and art. 12 (InfoLEG texto original) and Decreto 3213/84 art. 3 (texto actualizado) were read, and their dating is strong. I found no family-specific practice evidence for any period.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The answer holds, but the MRD's reading of art. 12 Ley 346 is wrong. It is a transitional clause of 1869 about children of native Argentines and foreigners then exercising citizenship, not automatic citizenship for children of citizens. Art. 2 inc. 2 point 7 literally covers men married to Argentine women; Decreto 3213/84 art. 3(f) extends the route to any spouse or native Argentine child.
answers.notes: The 'not the same' change reflects DNU 70/2017's narrowing of the general route (inc. 1), which family migrants also use. Their specific route (inc. 2 point 7; Decreto 3213/84 art. 3(f)) did not change between 2000 and 2020. If the reviewer treats only the family-specific route as decisive, 'no change' would be the alternative.
